topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: A parser can pass every unit test while a file adapter writes the wrong format or forgets to report a failed stream. Integration tests exercise those boundaries together. This chapter persists a bounded sequence of measurements, reloads it through the public adapter, and verifies both successful composition and a malformed-record failure.

topics.title: 7.1.1 Verifying Interface Contracts
topics.summary: An interface contract includes representation, ownership, error behavior, and limits. A writer and reader must agree on delimiters and numeric grammar, not merely on the fact that both use text. A network sender and receiver similarly need framing and byte-order agreement beyond sharing the type string.

topics.title: 7.2.1 Designing End-to-End Scenarios
topics.summary: An end-to-end scenario starts from a supported user entry point and checks an externally observable result. For a command-line program, that includes arguments, input files, standard output, standard error, exit status, and any created artifacts. Testing only a library function does not establish the CLI’s behavior.

blocks.text: Purpose
rich: Purpose

blocks.text: An end-to-end test treats the built application as a user would: invoke the executable, provide a fixture, and validate externally observable behavior.
rich: An end-to-end test treats the built application as a user would: invoke the executable, provide a fixture, and validate externally observable behavior.

blocks.text: Code or command
rich: Code or command

blocks.text:
set -euo pipefail
output=$(./app --input fixtures/valid.txt)
status=$?
printf 'status=%s output=%s\n' "$status" "$output"
test "$status" -eq 0
test "$output" = "records=3"

blocks.text: The save routine validates all values before opening the destination, reducing one class of destructive failure. Integration testing should state which of those guarantees is actually implemented.
